headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from MemMachine MCP plus Plane file/workspace handling; no direct write-conflict evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so its outputs can be bridged into Plane workflows. Plane accepts file uploads and handles hyperlinks/notes, which creates a plausible content-to-instruction path if Plane treats imported content as trusted. No direct evidence of a shared channel or parser hardening is provided, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plane ingests MemMachine-generated text from MCP, uploads, or notes without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF an operator manually copies MemMachine output into Plane task fields, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Disable automatic import of MemMachine output into Plane fields.
Add a review step before pasting or syncing content.
Restrict Plane file uploads to trusted sources only.
Use a prompt-injection filter on any MemMachine-to-Plane connector.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has allowlisted network egress; Plane handles files, notes, and hyperlinks with broad egress. If either side forwards shared content into the other’s backend or external services, sensitive context can leak across systems. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or same OAuth principal, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is copied into Plane issues or notes, both systems will retain the same sensitive facts.
IF Plane file uploads contain MemMachine-derived artifacts, those contents may be exposed to Plane's backend or integrations.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive MemMachine context into Plane tickets.
Redact personal facts before syncing notes or files.
Limit Plane uploads to non-sensitive artifacts.
Review outbound integrations on both systems.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class tagging and DLP on the connector.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has no filesystem write capability listed, while Plane explicitly has write_filesystem=false and supports multiple instances. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely from the profiles alone. The only plausible overlap is indirect through APIs or shared external resources, which is not enough to raise severity.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable external resource through an orchestrator, conflicts can appear.
IF an operator grants Plane filesystem write outside the profile, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Use per-agent API credentials.
Serialize any manual handoff between agents.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared external resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit conversational outputs through MCP/API, and Plane is an issue/task system that can store those outputs as notes, issues, or hyperlinks. If Plane treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors can cascade into task creation or scheduling decisions. Plane is not documented here as verifying upstream claims, so the pathway exists in default workflows but is not proven severe.
conditions: IF Plane users convert MemMachine output into issues or tasks without verification, downstream errors propagate.
IF MemMachine generates incorrect travel facts that Plane stores as authoritative notes, the error persists.
mitigations: Require human verification before creating Plane tasks from MemMachine output.
Mark imported content as untrusted in Plane.
Separate factual notes from actionable tasks.
Add source links to every imported item.
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks in the handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while Plane handles files, issues, and notes. The profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches, so there is no direct compliance breach evidenced. Because both can store user data and the interaction is undocumented, only a low residual compliance risk is justified.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is copied from MemMachine into Plane, retention and access policies must align.
IF Plane file uploads include sensitive user facts from MemMachine, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in Plane.
Delete duplicated records promptly.
Review retention settings in both systems.
Restrict access to imported notes and files.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention for the integration.
